text: How does ZFC block Russell's paradox?
choices: By declaring R = {x : x ∉ x} to be true rather than false
By replacing unrestricted comprehension with Separation, {x ∈ A : φ(x)}, which only filters an already-existing set A
By adding an axiom asserting a universal set of all sets
By forbidding the membership relation ∈ between sets
explanation: ZFC uses the Axiom of Separation (restricted comprehension): you may only carve {x ∈ A : φ(x)} out of an existing set A, never collect all x satisfying φ from nothing. Forming Russell's R would require a universal 'set of all sets,' which ZFC never provides. Option C is the opposite of ZFC (there is no universal set), and ∈ certainly still relates sets.
